key_results.text: Genie is the first generative interactive environment trained in an unsupervised manner from unlabelled Internet videos.
The model can generate an endless variety of action-controllable virtual worlds described through text, synthetic images, photographs, and even sketches.
At 11B parameters, Genie can be considered a foundation world model.

Genie enables users to act in the generated environments on a frame-by-frame basis despite training without any ground-truth action labels or other domain-specific requirements typically found in the world model literature.
The resulting learned latent action space facilitates training agents to imitate behaviors from unseen videos, opening the path for training generalist agents of the future.

method.text: Genie is comprised of a spatiotemporal video tokenizer, an autoregressive dynamics model, and a simple and scalable latent action model.

paper_cards.title: GameFactory: Creating New Games with Generative Interactive Videos

key_results.text: GameFactory effectively generates open-domain action-controllable game videos, representing a significant step forward in AI-driven game generation. [Abstract]
The framework introduces GF-Minecraft, an action-annotated game video dataset without human bias, enabling precise control over both keyboard and mouse inputs. [Abstract]
GameFactory supports autoregressive generation for unlimited-length interactive videos. [Abstract]
A multi-phase training strategy with a domain adapter decouples game style learning from action control, achieving scene-generalizable action control. [Abstract]

method.text: GameFactory is a framework for action-controlled scene-generalizable game video generation. [Abstract]
It includes an action control module that enables precise control over both keyboard and mouse inputs. [Abstract]
The method leverages open-domain generative priors from pre-trained video diffusion models to enable the creation of entirely new and diverse games beyond fixed styles and scenes. [Abstract]
A domain adapter is proposed to bridge the domain gap between open-domain priors and small-scale game datasets. [Abstract]

paper_cards.title: GTBench: Uncovering the Strategic Reasoning Limitations of LLMs via Game-Theoretic Evaluations

key_results.text: LLMs have distinct behaviors regarding various gaming scenarios; for example, LLMs fail in complete and deterministic games yet they are competitive in probabilistic gaming scenarios. [P1]

Most open-source LLMs, e.g., CodeLlama-34b-Instruct and Llama-2-70b-chat, are less competitive than commercial LLMs, e.g., GPT-4, in complex games, yet the recently released Llama-3-70b-Instruct makes up for this shortcoming. [P1]
Code-pretraining greatly benefits strategic reasoning, while advanced reasoning methods such as Chain-of-Thought (CoT) and Tree-of-Thought (ToT) do not always help. [P1]
The paper characterizes the game-theoretic properties of LLMs, such as equilibrium and Pareto Efficiency in repeated games. [P1]
Detailed error profiles are provided for a better understanding of LLMs' behavior. [P1]

method.text: GTBench is proposed as a language-driven environment composing 10 widely recognized tasks, across a comprehensive game taxonomy: complete versus incomplete information, dynamic versus static, and probabilistic versus deterministic scenarios. [P1]

The paper evaluates LLMs' reasoning abilities in competitive environments through game-theoretic tasks, e.g., board and card games that require pure logic and strategic reasoning to compete with opponents. [P1]

paper_cards.title: Hunyuan-GameCraft: High-dynamic Interactive Game Video Generation with Hybrid History Condition

key_results.text: Hunyuan-GameCraft significantly outperforms existing models in advancing the realism and playability of interactive game video generation. [Abstract]

The model achieves fine-grained action control by unifying standard keyboard and mouse inputs into a shared camera representation space, facilitating smooth interpolation between various camera and movement operations. [Abstract]
A hybrid history-conditioned training strategy is proposed that extends video sequences autoregressively while preserving game scene information. [Abstract]

Model distillation is achieved to reduce computational overhead while maintaining consistency across long temporal sequences, making it suitable for real-time deployment in complex interactive environments. [Abstract]

The model is trained on a large-scale dataset comprising over one million gameplay recordings across over 100 AAA games, ensuring broad coverage and diversity, then fine-tuned on a carefully annotated synthetic dataset to enhance precision and control. [Abstract]
The curated game scene data significantly improves the visual fidelity, realism and action controllability. [Abstract]

method.text: Hunyuan-GameCraft unifies standard keyboard and mouse inputs into a shared camera representation space for fine-grained action control. [Abstract]
A hybrid history-conditioned training strategy is used to extend video sequences autoregressively while preserving game scene information. [Abstract]
Model distillation is employed to reduce computational overhead while maintaining consistency across long temporal sequences for real-time deployment. [Abstract]
The model is trained on a large-scale dataset of over one million gameplay recordings across over 100 AAA games and fine-tuned on a carefully annotated synthetic dataset. [Abstract]

setup.text: The model is trained on a large-scale dataset comprising over one million gameplay recordings across over 100 AAA games. [Abstract]
The model is fine-tuned on a carefully annotated synthetic dataset to enhance precision and control. [Abstract]

limitations.text: Current methods face limitations in dynamics, generality, long-term consistency, and efficiency, which limit the ability to create various gameplay videos. [Abstract]

paper_cards.title: PokeLLMon: A Human-Parity Agent for Pokemon Battles with Large Language Models

key_results.text: PokeLLMon achieves human-parity performance in tactical battle games, specifically in Pokemon battles. [Abstract]
PokeLLMon demonstrates human-like battle strategies and just-in-time decision making in online battles against humans. [Abstract]
PokeLLMon achieves a 49% win rate in Ladder competitions and a 56% win rate in invited battles. [Abstract]

method.text: PokeLLMon incorporates in-context reinforcement learning to iteratively refine its policy by consuming text-based feedback derived from battles. [Abstract]
PokeLLMon uses knowledge-augmented generation to retrieve external knowledge, counteract hallucination, and enable timely and proper actions. [Abstract]
PokeLLMon employs consistent action generation to mitigate the panic switching phenomenon when facing powerful opponents. [Abstract]
